context:
Goal: keep GitHub's branch list small, so sessions find work fast.
Problem (rule): cloud sessions cannot delete branches, and each way to fix that adds a new writer, which needs your word.
Based on (measured): at 14:21 CST the cloud link dropped a branch-delete push ("unexpected disconnect"). A new-branch push worked.
Based on (measured): origin has 2,338 branches: 1,715 plain, 331 archive/, 160 lane/.
Based on (read): your Oct 30 grant allows a delete only when the branch's last commit is on main or on an archive branch.
Departs from: main, where cloud deletes go to a session on your computer — adds a GitHub Actions workflow that deletes on GitHub's side.
Meanwhile: deletes wait; no other work waits on this.
holds: Which way a cloud session deletes a branch that your Oct 30 grant already allows it to delete.

options.gain: Deletes happen on their own, with no token of yours in any session.
options.how: A GitHub Actions workflow deletes, with GitHub's own token, only what the Oct 30 grant allows. It runs after each merge and on demand.
options.label: GitHub workflow (Recommended)
options.lose: One more workflow to keep, and a bug in it could delete a branch the grant allows but you wanted.

options.how: Put your own GitHub token in the cloud environment as a secret. Untested.
options.label: Your token as a cloud secret
options.lose: Every cloud session holds a write token of yours.

options.how: Cloud sessions keep sending deletes to a session on your computer.
options.label: Keep relaying
options.lose: Deletes happen only while your computer runs, so branches keep piling up.

reply: Closed by your 14:25 CST chat answer (relayed by the retrospective): "im good with either an actions workflow or a github token -- github token seems better? im very ambivalent to tokens being in all my cloud sessions its just a github token". Home: R45 in restart-plan. You make one GitHub token and add it to the cloud environment as SHIV_GITHUB_TOKEN; a session then tests one delete and one Projects read with it.
title: How should cloud sessions delete old branches?
why: Cloud sessions cannot delete a branch today, so 2,338 branches pile up on GitHub.
